name: Hawaii
dek: A US state sheet. Honolulu International Airport, WMO 91182; Honolulu and Maui have their own sheets.
paragraphs: Hawaii is a US state, not a country; this is its state sheet. The reference station is Honolulu International Airport, WMO 91182, height 2 m, on Oʻahu. Hilo and Līhuʻe have their own files and were not averaged in; the windward sides and the mountains are wetter or cooler than this table.

The highest average high in the table is 31.5 °C, in August. The lowest average low is 19.3 °C, in January. The wettest month by the precipitation column is March, at 59.8 mm, and the driest is June, at 12.6 mm.

climate.caption: Reference station: Honolulu International Airport, WMO 91182. Not a statewide average.
climate.note: World Meteorological Organization 1991–2020 climatological standard normals, distributed by NOAA NCEI. Monthly values are copied as printed, with leading spaces removed; a value printed with no leading zero, such as -.3, is shown as -0.3.
climate.sourceTitle: WMO climate normals 1991-2020, Honolulu International Airport (91182)

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type A and B, 120 V, 60 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list, in the copy archived on 16 August 2026, shows United States at the voltage, frequency, and plug types in the figure. A direct download of the live page did not return the list, so the archive is the copy that was read.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: Section 291C-41 of the Hawaii Revised Statutes, on the Legislature's site, says that on all roadways of sufficient width a vehicle shall be driven on the right half of the roadway, with exceptions such as overtaking, obstructions, three-lane roads, and one-way roads.
driving.sourceTitle: Hawaii Revised Statutes 291C-41, Hawaii State Legislature

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.detail: Visit The USA, run by Brand USA, says diners usually tip 15–20% for a sit-down meal and 10% at a buffet, and that some restaurants add a gratuity for parties of six or more. Its same answer gives bartenders $1 a drink or 15–20%, taxis 10–18%, bell staff $1–2 a bag, housekeeping $2–5 a night, and tour guides 10–20%. It is guidance, not a law.
tipping.sourceTitle: Visit The USA (Brand USA), Travel Trade FAQ

water.label: Tap water
water.value: Safe to drink, per Visit The USA
water.detail: Visit The USA, run by Brand USA, says: "Protected by federal law, water in the United States is safe to drink." This is the tourism body's line, not a CDC or EPA statement, and local advisories can still apply.
water.sourceTitle: Visit The USA (Brand USA), Travel Trade FAQ

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the US Dollar, code USD, for the United States of America. It also lists US Dollar (Next day), code USN, a funds code, which is not printed as the currency.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone.tab gives the United States 29 rows. Pacific/Honolulu is commented Hawaii. The other US rows are not collapsed into it.

entry.label: Official entry requirements
entry.note: CBP's page for international visitors. It applies to travelers arriving from outside the United States. We do not restate a visa rule.

bestTime.intro: Month by month for Honolulu, from the station table above and two National Weather Service pages. The NWS Honolulu office's Climate of Hawaiʻi page says most of Hawaii has only two seasons: "summer," between May and October, and "winter," between October and April, and that the heaviest rains come from winter storms between October and April. NOAA gives the central Pacific hurricane season as 1 June to 30 November, with July, August and September as the peak months. The airport is on the leeward side of Oʻahu; windward coasts and the mountains are wetter than this table.

months.note: Winter season. Average high 26.9 °C, low 19.3 °C, 46.7 mm. The lowest average high and the lowest average low in the Honolulu table.

Winter season. Average high 27.0 °C, low 19.5 °C, 49.4 mm. The NWS page names February and March as Hawaii's coolest months and puts the lowest sea-surface temperature, 73 or 74 °F, between late February and March; at this station January's averages are slightly lower.
Winter season. Average high 27.3 °C, low 20.1 °C, 59.8 mm, the wettest month in the Honolulu table.
The last month of the NWS winter season. Average high 28.4 °C, low 21.1 °C, 19.5 mm, about a third of March's total.
The NWS summer season begins. Average high 29.3 °C, low 22.0 °C, 20.8 mm.
Summer season; the central Pacific hurricane season opens on 1 June. Average high 30.5 °C, low 23.2 °C, 12.6 mm, the driest month in the table.
Summer season and the first of NOAA's three peak hurricane months. Average high 31.2 °C, low 23.9 °C, 13.2 mm.
Summer season, peak hurricane months. Average high 31.5 °C, low 24.2 °C, 21.4 mm: the highest average high and low in the table. The NWS page names August and September as Hawaii's warmest months.

Summer season, the last of the peak hurricane months. Average high 31.3 °C, low 23.8 °C, 22.3 mm. The NWS page puts the highest sea-surface temperature, near 80 °F, in late September or early October.
The NWS page uses October as the turn from summer to winter. Average high 30.5 °C, low 23.3 °C, 38.3 mm. Still inside the hurricane season.
Winter season; the hurricane season closes on 30 November. Average high 29.0 °C, low 22.1 °C, 57.1 mm.
Winter season. Average high 27.7 °C, low 20.7 °C, 55.3 mm.
